components.gap: Mundici Section 1 (pp. 212-217, 1985 Springer printing) is reconstructed only for Definition 1.1.1, the logic L^R and its row semantics, the uniformization reading, Theorem 1.1.2 with a written proof, and the Q_0-definability display of Section 1.3 (p. 216) with proof. Missing, each with exact hypotheses, complete proof, examples and failure boundary: Walkoe's observation that L(Q^H) <= L(Q) for every partially ordered Q with L(Q) not equal to L_omega-omega (Q^H the weakest partially ordered quantifier) and Vaananen's result that no generalized quantifier Q has L(Q) = full second-order logic (p. 214); Theorem 1.2.1 (L^R equivalent to L(Q^H) over first-order Peano arithmetic) with its pairing-function and two-row reduction proof, and the Remark extending it to any first-order theory with a definable pairing function; Theorem 1.2.2 (Delta L(Q^H) = Delta L^R = Delta L^mII) with Claim 1 (L^R <=_RPC L^mII) and Claim 2 (L^mII <=_RPC L(Q^H)) and their proofs (pp. 214-215); Corollary 1.2.3 (same Lowenheim and Hanf numbers, recursively isomorphic sets of valid sentences) with proof; Remark 1.2.4; Proposition 1.3.1 (L(Q^H) neither (omega,omega)-compact nor axiomatizable, and without the weak Beth property) with proof; Theorem 1.3.2 in full (L(Q^H) >= L(Q_alpha) iff alpha = 0), including the proof of the only-if direction by induction on pure-identity formulas with Lowenheim-Skolem.

Mundici Section 3, Cardinality, Equivalence, Order Quantifiers and All That (pp. 225-232), is absent from the handbook route: no Theorem 3.1.1 (i)-(iii) (compact Delta-closed or interpolating logics generated by quantifiers that are classes of sets collapse to L_omega-omega; non-Delta-closure) with Lemma 3.1.2 and proofs, Theorem 3.1.3 (compact logics with interpolation and the Feferman-Vaught property) with its case proof, Theorem 3.1.4, the order quantifiers of Section 3.2 (Q^cf, Q^D, the well-ordering quantifier W) with Theorems 3.2.1, 3.2.2 and 3.2.3 (i)-(vi), Section 3.3 (Definition 3.3.1 of inductive classes, Theorems 3.3.2 and 3.3.3), and the open problem on extensions of L(Q^cf) satisfying Robinson's consistency theorem kept as an open question, each with exact hypotheses, complete proof, examples and failure boundary.
